summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 37.2% to ₹144.98 crore and PAT grew 171% to ₹8.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25.7%.
summary.overview: Shree Vasu Logistics reported strong H1 FY27 (half year ended 30 September 2026) standalone results, with revenue from operations up 37.2% YoY and EBITDA up 38.6%. Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹80.2 crore grew 43.2% YoY and 23.9% QoQ, while Q2 EBITDA margin eased to 25.6% from 25.8% in Q1. Management attributed growth to new client wins, repeat business in new territories, and added leadership in execution. The call was brief, and Q&A was mostly from individual participants on client concentration, M&A, fleet and EV plans, and insurance.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹13.6 crore YoY; margin 25.6% vs 25.8% in Q1
vs ₹1.2 crore YoY; vs ₹3.3 crore in Q1

segments.name: Third-party logistics (3PL)
segments.commentary: Covers CNF and depot operations, in-plant logistics, secondary transportation, and e-commerce and quick-commerce infrastructure. No segment-wise revenue split was given on the call.

segments.name: Secondary transportation (PTL)
segments.commentary: Combines own fleet with partner vehicles. Management said about 125 owned vehicles are used, with market-hired and contract transporters and couriers for smaller loads. No segment-wise revenue split was given.

segments.name: Warehouse leasing
segments.commentary: Described as steady annuity-style income. The company has 2.6 million sq ft of warehousing space. No segment-wise revenue split was given.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance was given for FY27 revenue, margin, or capex.
Management expects client base to keep broadening, with new clients added continuously alongside repeat business from clients in new territories.
Company plans to scale up in all zones over the coming months, with regional team setups in place across India.
Strategy: expand warehousing in high-demand zones, adopt supply chain automation, and deepen relationships with marquee enterprise clients.
EV fleet adoption is slow for now because acquisition and running costs are above normal vehicles; the company may shift when costs are back-to-back covered by clients.
capex_capacity: Footprint: operations in 16 states and 1 union territory across 43 cities, with 2.6 million sq ft of warehousing space.

Fleet: 100-plus owned vehicles per the prepared remarks; a participant cited 750 vehicles, and the answer put owned fleet at about 125 and said other modes are market-hired, contract transporters and couriers. The two fleet figures were not reconciled on the call.
Plan to scale up warehousing footprints in high-demand zones; no capex amount or commissioning timeline was disclosed.
Over 10,000 trained employees and a proprietary technology stack that supports zero-phone-call operations.
demand_pricing: Client base: about 136 enterprise clients; around 30% of business comes from the top 20 clients.
Named clients include Dabur, Parle, and JK Tyres, which are served across multiple locations.
Management said growth came from a strong order book from new clients and repeat business from existing clients in new territories.
Management said it was able to turn around new business started in the prior year.
Pricing and realisation commentary was not discussed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the client book, and what is the renewal and churn experience with legacy clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 136 clients, with about 30% of business from the top 20. Management said the company is not dependent on one or two clients and that the business is long-term and does not rely on renewal activity, since it holds large stock for clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company evaluating acquisitions, and how does it weigh inorganic growth against greenfield capacity given leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to acquisition offers but is focused on organic growth for now. Leverage was not discussed.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the fleet is owned versus attached or hired, what is utilisation, and what is the EV plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 125 vehicles are owned and the rest are market-hired on a day-to-day basis, with contract transporters and couriers for small loads. EVs have been deployed, but cost is higher, so the company is going slow and will decide on a comparative cost basis. Utilisation was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What are the insurance coverage and claim experience for vehicles, and is there any GST exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one or two accident incidents occur in a year across India. Clients' invoices cover the goods, and the client's survey insurer handles claims. Management said there is no GST demand on this.

risks_watch: Client concentration: about 30% of revenue from the top 20 clients, and no client-level detail was disclosed.
Fleet dependence on market-hired vehicles, which may be exposed to availability and cost pressure.
EV transition costs remain above conventional vehicles, which may delay fleet modernisation.
Q2 EBITDA margin dipped QoQ to 25.6% from 25.8% even as revenue rose 23.9%.
Leverage and capex funding were not discussed, even though an investor asked about them.
Participant-cited fleet size of 750 vehicles versus about 125 owned plus hired capacity was not clarified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the numbers and growth momentum, but brief and thin on detail. Management was direct on client concentration and EV timing, but gave few specifics on capex, leverage, or fleet size.
key_quotes: So, things that drove this performance was our strong order book for new clients, and at the same time, we strengthened our execution part by adding strong leaders in our company.
So, technically speaking, we are not dependent on any, one or two clients.
So, we are open to acquisition offers, but as of now, a lot of organic growth is coming in for us, so we are focusing on that.

adds.what: Plan to scale warehousing footprint in high-demand zones (no quantity given)

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given; management cited a strong order book from new clients and repeat business in new territories, and plans to scale warehousing in high-demand zones with no capex, size or timeline disclosed.
